bullets: Scrooge’s room transformed: holly, ivy, a blazing fire and a heap of food ‘to form a kind of throne’.
The Ghost: ‘a jolly Giant’, green robe, bare chest, holding a torch like Plenty’s horn: generosity, abundance, openness.
‘Come in! and know me better, man!’
Streets: shops overflowing, lists of fruit and food (‘blooming pyramids’), people cheerful in the cold: shared joy.
The Ghost sprinkles incense from his torch on the poor people’s dinners: blessing the poor most.
Mrs Cratchit ‘dressed out but poorly in a twice-turned gown, but brave in ribbons, which are cheap and make a goodly show’: dignity in poverty.
Tiny Tim arrives on Bob’s shoulder; his hope that people at church will remember Christ’s miracles.
The goose and pudding: modest food celebrated with joy.
Bob’s toast to ‘the Founder of the Feast’; Mrs Cratchit’s anger at Scrooge.
Scrooge asks if Tiny Tim will live: the Ghost repeats ‘surplus population’.
Miners, a lighthouse, a ship at sea: Christmas spirit everywhere.
Fred’s party: laughter, games, pity for Scrooge; Scrooge joins in invisibly.
Ignorance and Want: ‘wretched, abject, frightful, hideous, miserable’; ‘This boy is Ignorance. This girl is Want. Beware them both’; ‘Are there no prisons? Are there no workhouses?’

callouts.p: It shows that joy is possible even in poverty, then ends with the starkest warning in the novella: society’s neglect creates Ignorance and Want, and the rich are responsible.

exam.q: Explore how Dickens presents the Cratchit family in this extract (Stave 3, the Christmas dinner). (20 marks)
exam.tip: Comment on the narrator’s warmth: it shapes how we see the poor.

mistakes.r: It ends with the darkest social warning in the book.

quotes.q: Come in! and know me better, man!
brave in ribbons, which are cheap and make a goodly show

summary: Stave 3 extracts cover the Ghost of Christmas Present and the abundant streets, the Cratchits’ Christmas dinner and Tiny Tim, Fred’s party, and Ignorance and Want; learn how Dickens combines joy with social warning.

terms.d: Placing contrasting things side by side (feast and Ignorance and Want).
